clue.text: FT compilers sleeping around were cruel to partners!

indicators.note: around tells us the word for sleeping wraps itself round the compilers

parts.note: sleeping means in bed, abed
the setter speaks for the FT's team of compilers, who would call themselves us

explanation.surface: A scandalous claim that the newspaper's crossword setters slept around and mistreated their spouses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface libels the setters themselves; the whole clue also reads as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating a partner cruelly is ill-treatment, which is what abuse of a spouse amounts to.

clue.text: Nonsensical writer in Times with tired eyes

indicators.note: in places the writer inside the word for times

parts.note: times as in multiplication, three by four, gives by
Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussycat

explanation.surface: A writer of nonsense working at The Times, worn out and bleary-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign read as BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and watery from fatigue, so a synonym of tired-eyed.

clue.text: Pigs at the dance seeking meal

indicators.note: to dance is to move about, so the letters of the three words jig into a new order

explanation.surface: Hungry pigs at a dance on the lookout for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is well hidden because 'Pigs at the' reads as ordinary sentence words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of pasta strands is an example of a meal.

clue.text: Sketch has detainee in row over Pound

indicators.note: a row is a noisy quarrel, so the letters are in disorder and must be rearranged

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A drawing shows a prisoner caught up in a quarrel about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in row' rearranges DETAINEE plus L into the answer; 'Pound' looks like the poet or the verb but is the money sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to draw or outline, the verb sense of sketch.

clue.text: An idea if seal be broken

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'An idea if seal be broken (8)': anagram of IF SEAL BE gives FEASIBLE, but 'An idea' cannot define an adjective meaning achievable; the defining word appears to be missing.
annotationWithheld.clue: An idea if seal be broken

clue.text: As this answer will be written throughout?

definitions.text: As this answer will be written throughout?

parts.words: As this answer will be written throughout?
parts.note: a down light is entered in the grid starting at its upper end and finishing at its lower end, and the phrase also means throughout

explanation.surface: A question about how the answer is going to be entered in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means 'entirely, throughout', and as a down entry it is literally written that way in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely or thoroughly, matching throughout, and also describes how a down entry is filled in.

clue.text: An Indian part in playing Casablancan pianist?

parts.note: an actor in playing Hamlet appears as Hamlet
Sam is the pianist in the film Casablanca, asked to play As Time Goes By

explanation.surface: An Indian actor's role in playing the piano man from Casablanca.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests casting an Indian actor; 'An Indian part' is actually a region of India, the tea-growing state.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, so a part of the country.

clue.text: Bury Football Club seen in Milan

definitions.meaning: to bury is to ... a body in the ground
Internazionale, known as ..., is one of the two big football clubs of Milan

explanation.surface: Bury FC, an English football club, spotted in Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town with an English football club, which makes the surface look like one sporting name.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter is a verb meaning to put a body in a grave, and also the short name of a Milanese club.

clue.text: Revolutionary — as 9 is in schedule!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Revolutionary - as 9 is in schedule! (8)': the blog's parse is NINE reversed inside LIST, but no word signals the reversal unless 'Revolutionary' serves as both definition and indicator.

clue.text: Queen stops fuels being thrown over Muslim wives

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the queen goes into a gap in the reversed fuels
thrown over means flipped end to end, so the fuels are read backwards

parts.note: oil and gas are two fuels
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A monarch halts the dumping of fuel supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being thrown over' reverses OIL GAS to SAGLIO, and 'stops' puts ER after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is a harem, the women's quarters of a Muslim household and, by extension, the wives in it.

clue.text: Bend to receive spank in Thai capital

indicators.note: the word for bend takes in, or receives, the word for spank

parts.note: to sag is to bend or droop
to tan someone's hide is to beat or spank them

explanation.surface: Bending over for a spanking in Bangkok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city, Bangkok, but means money: a satang is a hundredth of a baht.
explanation.definitionFit: The satang is a small coin of Thailand's currency, so a piece of Thai money.

clue.text: Roach cooked by new magistrate in Athens

indicators.note: cooked fish has been altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek magistrate served cooked roach, a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An archon was one of the chief magistrates of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Monkey departs tree

parts.note: a tamarin is a small South American monkey
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A monkey leaves a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The monkey leaving the tree is a natural picture; the tree is actually the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree grown for its pods.

clue.text: Left cuts excellent boxer

indicators.note: the letter for left cuts into the word for excellent, splitting it

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-rate

explanation.surface: A left that cuts open a fine fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was a heavyweight champion, an example of a famous boxer.

clue.text: Club bouncer is important in organisation that engages 50

indicators.note: engages means takes in, so the jumbled letters hold the numeral
being put into organisation means the letters are reorganised

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman matters in a firm that employs fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in organisation' rearranges IS IMPORTANT, and 'that engages' puts L into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast who bounces on a trampoline, perhaps in a club, is someone who bounces.

clue.text: Terrible rip in chair? I see what you're saying!

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the word for chair

parts.note: the chair of a meeting is its leader

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A nasty tear in the chair prompts an exclamation of understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' signals the anagram of the tear, and the chair is a meeting's head, not furniture; the exclamation pictures someone who sees speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reading lips literally sees speech, so 'I see what you're saying' is a witty description.

clue.text: See 5
Suspect price I probed is work of fiction

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or questionable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A dodgy price someone investigated turns out to be invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like an investigator's word, chiming with 'probed', but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice-ripper is a racy historical romance novel, a kind of fiction.

clue.text: Disagreeable woman to frighten as with threats

definitions.meaning: an unpleasant woman can be called this, a farmyard insult
to intimidate or browbeat someone into submission

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is slang for an unpleasant woman; as a verb it means to intimidate.

clue.text: Muslim claim is falsely made

indicators.note: something put falsely is misrepresented, so the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A claim made falsely about something Muslim.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic is the adjective for the religion of Islam, so it means Muslim.

clue.text: A wall painting put up causes conflict

indicators.note: in a down entry put up means written bottom to top, so the painting is reversed

parts.note: a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: Hanging a wall painting starts a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' sounds like hanging the picture, but in a down clue it means the painting is written upwards. Alarum is the old stage direction in 'alarums and excursions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarum is an old word for a call to arms or noise of battle, as in Shakespeare's stage direction 'alarums and excursions'.

clue.text: Land with everyone going after sentimental stuff

indicators.note: going after places the second pieces behind the first

parts.note: corn is mawkish, sentimental material
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A country where everyone chases soppy sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is a county of England, a region or tract of land.

clue.text: Cleverly simple opener from Huddersfield Town

parts.note: a neat solution is cleverly simple

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A simply clever goal opens the scoring for Huddersfield Town, a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Huddersfield Town is an English football club, so 'Town' looks part of its name; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town in south Wales.

clue.text: Books to get on earlier vehicle

indicators.note: earlier puts this piece first in the down entry

parts.note: to get on is to grow older, to age
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Books getting on an earlier bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' means a means or medium: an agent is the instrument through which something is done.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is a means by which something is achieved, the figurative sense of vehicle.

clue.text: Prince Henry in Devonian river to send forth wind

indicators.note: in places the prince inside the river

parts.note: the Exe flows through Devon to Exeter
Hal is Prince Henry in Shakespeare's Henry IV

explanation.surface: A prince in a Devon river breaking wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, sending air from the lungs.

clue.text: Our planes, on time in south-east, use machine-guns

indicators.note: in puts the combined pieces inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: on means placed next to, here with the planes after the time

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are Britain's own aircraft

explanation.surface: British warplanes arrive on time over south-east England and open fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack from low-flying aircraft with gunfire.

clue.text: Doctor saves nothing on average

indicators.note: saves means keeps safe within, so the doctor holds the zero

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
O, the zero, means nothing
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A doctor who rescues nobody is just average.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means ordinary, only of middling quality.

clue.text: City welcomes politician with role, one speaking firmly

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the City letters enclose the rest

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
MP, Member of Parliament
a hat is a role, as in wearing another hat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The City greets an MP in a new role who speaks firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means forceful, expressing something with emphasis.

clue.text: Said to be spacious, but damp and unhealthy

indicators.note: said signals the clue word should be heard, not read

parts.note: roomy means spacious

explanation.surface: Somewhere reputedly spacious that is actually damp and unhealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumy describes air that is cold and damp, or watery eyes, both linked to ill health.
